sami: Heads-up — ran a multi-model co-residency run on a p4d node (2 models: 13B chat and a dense 3B reranker) and hit a repeatable OOM during high-concurrency bursts. Repro steps + profile attached in the artifacts link. Thinking of landing an "adaptive-slab-lanes" allocator patch that does two things: (1) keep a small always-resident lane for KV+critical activations, and (2) use a softer eviction score that prefers dropping non-hot KV pages first. Results so far look promising but need extra eyes before canary. TL;DR: dramatic drop in OOMs, slight p95 latency increase.

helen: saw the run. nice catch. can you paste the flamegraph snippet? also curious if kernel selection hysteresis (switching kernels only after sustained perf delta) played a part here — we saw jitter swapping kernels can spike memory.

sami: pasted snippet below (trimmed):

```
flamegraph: co-res-run-2026-03-16.svg
hot spots:
- kv_cache_copy: 28% (spiky during batch boundary)
- alloc_slab: 22% (many small allocs -> fragmentation)
- attention_kernel_fallback: 10% (fallback path allocs temp buff)
```

sami: hypothesis: the alloc pattern for the 13B chat produces many mid-sized workspace allocations that fragment the slab. When kernel fallback happens (larger temp buffers), combined working set + KV causes transient oversubscription. adaptive-slab-lanes reduces fragmentation and gives KV a protected residency.

raj: quick numbers from my local run with the patch:
- baseline: 9 OOMs / 1000 high-concurrency requests
- adaptive-slab-lanes + kv-soft-evict: 1 OOM / 1000 (89% reduction)
- p95 latency: baseline 78ms -> patched 82ms (4ms up), p50 unchanged

raj: key change: set workspace_min=16MB for medium allocs so we don't create a bazillion 1MB fragments. also added an eviction weight multiplier for kv pages (kv_weight=0.6) so activations score higher for eviction.

miles: nice. did you also change batching hints? earlier we had aggressive dynamic batching that amplified the spike when kernels switched.

sami: yes — two batching heuristics tuned:
1) batch_hint_threshold: avoid increasing batch size during kernel fallback windows.
2) preemptive_kv_restore: if slot reclaim would evict KV for an in-flight request, we attempt an async restore before completing the batch.

helen: any perf regressions in throughput after these changes? we need to measure token/sec under steady state.

raj: steady-state throughput is flat within noise (+1.2% at 95% conf). the regression is only during tail bursts where we trade a few ms latency for reduced OOMs. long-term the lower eviction churn improves overall throughput since we avoid GC/restore cycles.

ci-bot: perf-run #2482 finished.
- tests: cohost-13b-3b-highq
- result: PASS (regression threshold: p95 latency <= +10ms, OOM <= 0.5%)
- artifacts: https://ci.internal/runs/2482/artifacts

miles: can we get a microbench for kernel selection hysteresis? i want to see memory churn vs kernel switch threshold. if hysteresis is too low we keep flipping kernels and that creates temporary buffers.

sami: created a microbench script: `tools/bench/kernel-switch-hysteresis.py` (params: hysteresis_ms, batch_size, seq_len). Quick try: hysteresis_ms=200 reduced switches by ~75% in the hot path and eliminated the fallback buffer spike.

helen: two suggestions before canary:
- add observability: delta-metrics for "kv-evicted-by-alloc" and "kernel-switch-count" exposed in console per model route.
- safe-fallback: if we ever hit >2 evictions/sec for a model, temporarily pin it to a smaller model variant (auto-fallback) instead of allowing repeated restores.

sami: agreed. I'll add the metrics and the auto-fallback rule config.

raj: rollout plan:
- canary 2% traffic on Dedicated pool A with metric alarms: OOM, p98 latency, kernel-switch-count.
- if stable after 24h, bump to 25% and run perf soak 48h.

miles: also add an A/B with the old allocator for 6h so we can compare real workload regression.

sami: will do. i'll open the PR with tests and the canary config. assigning reviewers @helen @raj. thanks all :rocket:

ci-bot: PR #6421 opened by sami -> https://git.internal/pulls/6421 (includes bench, unit tests, perf job)

helen: quick nit on PR — can we make `kv_weight` configurable per-model? some rerankers prefer larger KV residency.

sami: yes, default 0.6, can override in route config. I'll update.

miles: 👍 let's keep an eye on the canary graphs. if we see any kernel-switch storm, revert and iterate.

raj: one more note — documented the recovery path in runbook: if canary starts evicting >5 KV/sec, trigger immediate rollback and open incident. I'll add the steps.

sami: thanks — closing for now, will post canary update in this thread.
